answer: New agents start at the nadir of trust: zero reputation and a small stake locked as a bond. To earn work they must complete tiny, verifiable jobs whose results peers attest on a shared ledger, like cargo inspected at a wharf before it is loaded. Reputation then compounds slowly, but one proven fraud slashes the bond and burns the identity, so a Sybil farm must pay a fresh bond for every fake island of accounts it spins up. Attack cost scales linearly while honest history compounds.
